questions.question: Before deploying a workplace-monitoring AI, a company must systematically document the privacy risks and mitigations, as the GDPR requires for high-risk processing. Which assessment framework does it conduct?
questions.explanation: A DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment) is the structured risk assessment the GDPR mandates before processing likely to result in high risk to individuals.

questions.question: A released dataset claims k-anonymity on quasi-identifiers (age, ZIP, sex). Every equivalence class has at least 10 records except one class that has only 2. What k does the dataset actually achieve?
questions.explanation: k-anonymity is set by the smallest equivalence class; one class of just 2 records caps the guarantee at 2-anonymity regardless of the others.

questions.question: A promotion model selects 30% of male and 30% of female candidates, though its error rates differ between the groups. Which fairness criterion is satisfied because the selection rates are equal?
questions.explanation: Demographic (statistical) parity requires only equal positive-selection rates across groups; it ignores error rates, unlike equalized odds.

questions.question: A retailer processes customer purchase data for fraud prevention without consent, after a documented balancing test showing its security interest outweighs the impact on customers' rights. Which GDPR lawful basis applies?
questions.explanation: Legitimate interest permits processing without consent when a genuine organizational need outweighs individual rights, documented via a balancing test.

questions.question: Five hospitals want a shared diagnostic model but cannot pool patient records; each trains the model locally and only model updates are aggregated on a central server. What technique is this?
questions.explanation: Federated learning keeps raw data on each site and aggregates only model updates, enabling joint training without centralizing data.

questions.question: A k-anonymous dataset is still vulnerable because every record in one equivalence class shares the same sensitive diagnosis. Which property requires each class to contain at least l well-represented distinct sensitive values?
questions.explanation: L-diversity extends k-anonymity by requiring each equivalence class to contain at least l distinct, well-represented sensitive values, blocking homogeneity attacks.

questions.question: A forum is sued over a defamatory post written by one of its users. Which US legal doctrine shields the platform from liability for that user-generated content?
alternatives: Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act
questions.explanation: Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act immunizes online platforms from liability for content posted by their users.

questions.question: A loan model must have both its false-positive rate and its false-negative rate equal across ethnic groups — not merely equal approval rates. Which fairness criterion is required?
questions.explanation: Equalized odds requires equal true-positive and false-positive rates across groups, a stricter criterion than equal opportunity (TPR only) or demographic parity (selection rates only).

questions.question: A cloud service computes the average of salary figures that stay encrypted the entire time; the server never sees plaintext. Which cryptographic technique makes this possible?
questions.explanation: Homomorphic encryption allows arithmetic on ciphertexts whose decryption matches the result on the plaintexts, so computation never exposes raw data.

questions.question: An l-diverse dataset still leaks information because each equivalence class's diagnosis distribution skews differently from the population's. Which property bounds the distance between each class's sensitive-value distribution and the global one?
questions.explanation: T-closeness requires the sensitive-attribute distribution within each equivalence class to stay within distance t of the overall distribution, defeating skewness and background-knowledge attacks.

questions.question: A hiring model trained on past decisions rejects more women; what type of bias is this?
questions.explanation: Historical bias reproduces past discrimination embedded in the data.

questions.question: A customer is denied a loan entirely by an algorithm with no human involvement and demands meaningful human review of that decision. Which GDPR provision protects her?
questions.explanation: Article 22 grants the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, including the right to obtain human intervention.

questions.question: An attacker trains shadow models to learn a target model's confidence patterns, then determines whether a specific patient's record was in its training set. What attack is this?
questions.explanation: Membership inference exploits differences in model behavior on seen versus unseen records to decide whether a given record was part of training.

questions.question: An 'anonymized' medical dataset is joined with public voter-registration records via ZIP code, birthdate, and sex, re-identifying patients. What attack does this describe?
questions.explanation: A linkage attack joins quasi-identifiers in a released dataset with an external source to re-identify individuals.

questions.question: A bank wants equal approval rates for qualified applicants across groups; which fairness criterion equalizes true positive rates?
questions.explanation: Equal opportunity requires equal true positive rates across groups.

questions.question: A released hospital dataset guarantees that every combination of quasi-identifiers (age, ZIP, sex) appears in at least 7 records. What privacy property does it satisfy, and at what level?
questions.explanation: k-anonymity requires each equivalence class of quasi-identifiers to contain at least k records; here k = 7.

questions.question: A lender approves 80% of male applicants but only 56% of female applicants. The ratio 56/80 = 0.7 falls below 0.8. Which fairness guideline from US employment law is failed?
questions.explanation: The EEOC's four-fifths rule presumes adverse impact when a group's selection rate is below 80% of the highest group's rate.

questions.question: Under the GDPR, a user demands all their personal data in a structured, machine-readable format so they can transfer it to another service. Which right is being exercised?
questions.explanation: Article 20 of the GDPR grants data subjects the right to receive their data in a portable, machine-readable format.

questions.question: A counting query on a medical database has sensitivity 1. A differentially private system uses the Laplace mechanism with epsilon = 0.5. What scale parameter b does the added noise use?
questions.explanation: The Laplace mechanism draws noise with scale b = sensitivity / epsilon = 1 / 0.5 = 2.

questions.question: An attacker repeatedly queries a face-recognition model and reconstructs images resembling a specific person's training photos. What class of attack is this?
questions.explanation: Model inversion exploits model outputs to reconstruct or approximate the training data associated with a target.
